sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐秘.

sentences.en: Hear something called the Vox Humana.
sentences.zh: 听听这个被称为“人声”的节目.

sentences.en: Involved the audience far more than television ever did.
sentences.zh: 它比电视以往任何时候都更能吸引观众的参与.

sentences.en: And here's some more hit music.
sentences.zh: 接下来还有更多热门音乐.

sentences.en: On our way to Canaan land.
sentences.zh: 走在通往迦南美地的路上.

sentences.en: There are those innovations that everyone loves and depends on.
sentences.zh: 有些创新是每个人都喜爱并依赖的.

sentences.en: Your biggies, like computers, electricity, the printing press.
sentences.zh: 比如你们熟知的大发明，电脑、电力、印刷机.

sentences.en: And then there are the innovations that made you who you are.
sentences.zh: 然后是那些塑造了你之所为你的创新.

sentences.en: Punk rock music, photocopiers, cassettes, nunchucks.
sentences.zh: 朋克摇滚乐、复印机、磁带、双节棍.

sentences.en: But if I were to rank them, I think the two most important technological innovations to my life
sentences.zh: 但如果要我进行排名，我认为对我的一生而言最重要的两项技术创新

sentences.en: are broadcasting and home sound recording.
And today I have two of my favorite stories from two of my favorite indie productions
sentences.zh: 今天，我带来了两个我最喜欢的独立制作团队的故事

sentences.en: all about the early days of broadcasting and recording.
sentences.zh: 全部关于广播和录音的早期岁月.

sentences.en: Radiotopians, Radio Diaries, and the Kitchen Sisters represent the best of what we can achieve
sentences.zh: Radiotopia电台网、“无线电日记”和“厨房姐妹”代表了我们在
音频讲故事领域所能取得的最高成就.

sentences.en: And here they are tackling the subjects that are near and dear to my heart.
sentences.zh: 在这里，他们正在探讨我内心深处最关切的主题.

sentences.en: These pieces were first broadcast on NPR as part of the Kitchen Sisters Lost and Found Sound Series.
sentences.zh: 这些节目最初是在NPR作为“厨房姐妹寻声记”系列的一部分播出的.

sentences.en: First up, with his story of Conrad's Garage and the birth of commercial broadcasting
sentences.zh: 首先出场的是来自“无线电日记”的乔·里奇曼

sentences.en: in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, this is Joe Richman from Radio Diaries.
sentences.zh: 他带来了关于宾夕法尼亚州匹兹堡的康拉德车库与商业广播诞生的故事.

sentences.en: The sounds that came out of Frank Conrad's garage in 1919 and 1920 are gone.
sentences.zh: 1919年和1920年从弗兰克·康拉德的车库里传出的声音已经消失了.

sentences.en: There were no recordings made, and everyone who participated in those weekly broadcasts has died.
sentences.zh: 当时没有留下任何录音，所有参与过那些每周广播的人都已经去世了.

sentences.en: In fact, there may be only one person still alive who actually heard what was going on in that garage.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在这个世界上可能只剩下一个人还亲耳听过那个车库里发生的事情.
一个名叫哈里·米尔斯的男子.
你今天晚上过得怎么样？

sentences.en: He was an engineer for RCA most of his life, but for the last eight decades,
sentences.zh: 他大半辈子都是RCA的工程师，但在过去的八十年里

sentences.en: he's been going on the ham radio just about every day.
sentences.zh: 他几乎每天都在使用业余无线电台.
米尔斯在1919年首次接触到无线电.

sentences.en: He was 12 years old, and his parents bought him a copy of the Boy Scout Handbook.
sentences.zh: 他当时12岁，父母给他买了一本《童子军手册》.

sentences.en: In the book, after a lot of the camping and the setting up a tent in the rain
sentences.zh: 在书里，除了大量的露营、在雨中搭帐篷

sentences.en: and helping the old lady cross the street and so on,
sentences.zh: 以及扶老奶奶过马路等等内容之后

sentences.en: in the back was a chapter on how to build a wireless station.
sentences.zh: 书的背面有一个关于如何建造无线电台的章节.

sentences.en: I had never heard of such a thing, so I built one.
sentences.zh: 我以前从未听说过这种东西，所以我建了一个.

sentences.en: I'll show you how it works.
sentences.zh: 我来向你展示它是如何运作的.

sentences.en: It was built out of photograph plates and tinfoil, the condenser, and this is weatherstripping.
sentences.zh: 它是用照相底片和锡箔纸、电容器做成的，这部分是防风雨条.

sentences.en: And this is a Ford coil, Ford ignition coil, which would hook onto your antenna and you're on the air.
sentences.zh: 这是福特线圈，福特点火线圈，只要把它连到天线上，你就可以开始广播了.

sentences.en: This is what radio sounded like when Mills first started, the dots and dashes of Morse code.
sentences.zh: 这就是米尔斯刚开始接触无线电时听到的声音，莫尔斯电码的点与划.

sentences.en: That's the letter V, which you use for test purposes.
sentences.zh: 那是字母V，用于测试目的.

sentences.en: If he hears me, he'd come back and we'd hold a conversation, as simple as that.
sentences.zh: 如果他听到我，他就会回复，然后我们就可以对话，就这么简单.

sentences.en: Almost every night, Harry Mills would lie in his bed and listen to the amateur radio operator's signal back and forth.
sentences.zh: 几乎每天晚上，哈里·米尔斯都会躺在床上，收听业余无线电爱好者的信号来回传递.

sentences.en: Then one night, he heard something different.
sentences.zh: 直到有一天晚上，他听到了一些不同的声音.

sentences.en: I remember it was 10 or 11 o'clock at night, and all at once, this voice appears.
sentences.zh: 我记得那是深夜10点或11点，突然之间，这个声音出现了.

sentences.en: And I remember letting out a yelp or a shout of some sort, and my dad, who had just gotten out of the bath,
sentences.zh: 我记得自己发出了某种尖叫或喊声，我刚洗完澡的父亲

sentences.en: come in wrapped in a towel to be sure I was all right.
sentences.zh: 裹着浴巾跑进来确认我是否一切都好.

sentences.en: And I said, Dad, look, I'm hearing this fellow talking.
sentences.zh: 我说，爸爸，你看，我听到这家伙在说话.

sentences.en: We only had one pair of headphones.
And he yelled out as I was right.
sentences.zh: 当我发现自己猜对时，他大声喊了出来.

sentences.en: Harry Mills had stumbled onto the experimental transmissions coming from Frank Conrad's garage, 35 miles away.
sentences.zh: 哈里·米尔斯无意中收听到了来自35英里外弗兰克·康拉德车库的实验性广播.

sentences.en: He was talking, and he says, now I'm going to play a phonograph record.
sentences.zh: 他在说话，他说，现在我要播放一张留声机唱片.

sentences.en: I didn't know he could do that.
sentences.zh: 我不知道他还能这么做.

sentences.en: To begin with, I hadn't heard voice before.
sentences.zh: 首先，我以前从未听过声音.

sentences.en: And as I add that to music, it opens up a whole new world.
sentences.zh: 当我把这个和音乐结合起来时，它开启了一个全新的世界.

sentences.en: Frank Conrad was not the first person to talk and play music on the radio.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克·康拉德并不是第一个在无线电里说话和播放音乐的人.

sentences.en: Inventors like Reginald Fessenden, Lee de Forrest, and Marconi had been doing such experiments as early as 1906.
sentences.zh: 雷金纳德·费森день、李·德·福斯特和马可尼等发明家早在1906年就已经在进行此类实验了.

sentences.en: But back then, radio was seen as a method of one-to-one communication, like the telegraph.
sentences.zh: 但当时，无线电被视为一种点对点的通信方式，就像电报一样.

sentences.en: Few envisioned radio as a way to reach many people at the same time, to broadcaSt.
sentences.zh: 很少有人把无线电设想为一种能同时接触许多人、进行广播的途径.

sentences.en: Frank Conrad was among the first to use the word broadcasting.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克·康拉德是最早使用“广播”一词的人之一.

sentences.en: It was originally an agricultural term used to describe the distribution of seeds over a large area.
sentences.zh: 它最初是一个农业术语，用来描述在广阔土地上撒播种子.

sentences.en: In his garage, Conrad helped to change the concept of radio.
sentences.zh: 在他的车库里，康拉德帮助改变了无线电的概念.

sentences.en: And he did it largely by accident.
sentences.zh: 而他做到这一点很大程度上是个意外.

sentences.en: This is Frank Conrad from the garage.
sentences.zh: 我是来自车库的弗兰克·康拉德.

sentences.en: This is what it would have sounded like anyway.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，当时听起来大概就是这样.

sentences.en: It's probably fair to say that nobody cares more about Frank Conrad's garage than a man named Rick Harris.
sentences.zh: 这样说或许很公平：没有人比一个叫里克·哈里斯的人更关心弗兰克·康拉德的车库了.

sentences.en: Harris is an amateur historian who has dedicated his life to preserving and researching the history of that garage.
sentences.zh: 哈里斯是一名业余历史学家，他一生致力于保护和研究那个车库的历史.

sentences.en: He's collected replicas of the equipment Conrad used.
sentences.zh: 他收集了康拉德使用过的设备的复制品.

sentences.en: A microphone, made out of the top of a candlestick telephone, mounted in a small box stuffed with cotton.
sentences.zh: 一个由烛台式电话顶部制成的麦克风，安装在一个塞满棉花的的小盒子里.
还有一个手摇维克特罗拉留声机.

sentences.en: Rick Harris says the story of Frank Conrad's garage really begins with that Victrola.
sentences.zh: 里克·哈里斯说，弗兰克·康拉德车库的故事确实是从那台留声机开始的.

sentences.en: Conrad was an engineer for Westinghouse, so he had access to vacuum tubes, which allowed him to transmit his voice over the air.
sentences.zh: 康拉德是西屋电气公司的工程师，所以他能接触到真空管，这使他能够通过空气传播他的声音.

sentences.en: But at the time, Conrad wasn't thinking about broadcasting.
sentences.zh: 但当时，康拉德并没有考虑广播的事.

sentences.en: He was simply trying to test and improve his transmitting equipment.
sentences.zh: 他只是在尝试测试和改进他的发射设备.

sentences.en: The problem was his voice, after talking endless hours into the microphone, would wear out.
sentences.zh: 问题是他的声音在对着麦克风讲了无数个小时后会沙哑.

sentences.en: So he got the idea one day to put on a record that would give him two or three minutes to adjust his equipment and would save his voice.
sentences.zh: 所以有一天他萌生了一个想法，播放一张唱片可以给他两三分钟时间来调整设备，也能保护他的嗓子.

sentences.en: This one is an ancient one, so I don't know what it's going to sound like, though.
sentences.zh: 这张是很古老的唱片，所以我也不知道它听起来会怎么样.

sentences.en: And as soon as he started playing the music, he began getting requests for more music, and he would get phone calls and letters asking him to play a certain song at a certain time.
sentences.zh: 一旦他开始播放音乐，他就开始收到更多音乐的要求，他会接到电话和信件，要求他在特定时间播放某首特定的歌.

sentences.en: So someone listening with their crystal set could convince a relative that you could actually play music over the air.
sentences.zh: 因此，用矿石收音机收听的人可以向亲戚证明，你真的可以通过无线电播放音乐.

sentences.en: This is Frank Conrad, recorded in the late 1930s, not long before he died.
sentences.zh: 这是弗兰克·康拉德，录制于20世纪30年代末，在他去世不久前.

sentences.en: Over time, Conrad's garage started to sound more like a radio station.
sentences.zh: 随着时间推移，康拉德的车库听起来越来越像一个广播电台.

sentences.en: Along with phonograph records, Conrad would transmit piano solos by family members and baseball scores.
sentences.zh: 除了留声机唱片，康拉德还会播放家庭成员的钢琴独奏和棒球比分.

sentences.en: And then, when he started to run out of records to play, Conrad went to the Hamilton Music Store and asked if he could borrow some for his broadcasts.
sentences.zh: 然后，当他发现没有唱片可放时，康拉德去了汉密尔顿音乐商店，问是否可以借一些用于他的广播.

sentences.en: The owner said yes, as long as Conrad agreed to announce the name of the store on the air.
sentences.zh: 店主答应了，只要康拉德同意在广播中宣布店名.

sentences.en: Slowly, Conrad was building the one thing the radio industry hadn't yet thought much about, an audience.
sentences.zh: 慢慢地，康拉德正在建立一个当时广播行业还没有太在意的东西——听众群.

sentences.en: But the real turning point came on September 29, 1920, when the Joseph Horn Department Store placed this ad in the Pittsburgh Sun.
sentences.zh: 但真正的转折点发生在1920年9月29日，当时约瑟夫·霍恩百货公司在《匹兹堡太阳报》上刊登了这则广告.

sentences.en: Air concert picked up by radio here.
sentences.zh: 在此处通过无线电接收到的空中音乐会.

sentences.en: The music was from a Victrola, in the home of Frank Conrad.
sentences.zh: 音乐来自弗兰克·康拉德家中的一台维克特罗拉留声机.

sentences.en: Mr. Conrad is a wireless enthusiast and puts on the wireless concerts periodically for the entertainment of many people in this district who have wireless sets.
sentences.zh: 康拉德先生是一位无线电爱好者，他定期举办无线电音乐会，为本地区许多拥有无线电设备的人提供娱乐.

sentences.en: Amateur wireless sets are on sale here, $10 and up.
sentences.zh: 业余无线电设备在此出售，10美元起售.

sentences.en: The ad really caught the attention of Conrad's boss at Westinghouse, a man by the name of Harry Davis, who, the story goes, called Conrad in the next day, and said, essentially,
sentences.zh: 这则广告确实引起了康拉德在西屋公司的老板哈里·戴维斯的注意，据传说，他第二天把康拉德叫去，基本上这样说道：

sentences.en: I would like to put you out of business, because I would like Westinghouse to set up its own station.
sentences.zh: 我想让你关门大吉，因为我想让西屋公司建立自己的电台.

sentences.en: And Davis asked Conrad, could that be done?
sentences.zh: 戴维斯问康拉德，这能做到吗？
康拉德回答说，当然可以.

sentences.en: So, over the next month, Conrad and his team began constructing a wooden shack on the roof of the Westinghouse plant.
sentences.zh: 于是，在接下来的一個月里，康拉德和他的团队开始在西屋工厂的屋顶上建造一个木屋.
他们建造了一个100瓦的发射器.

sentences.en: on the night of November 2, 1920, the newly licensed station, KDKA, went on the air.
sentences.zh: 1920年11月2日的夜晚，新获得牌照的电台KDKA正式开播.

sentences.en: K.A., of the Westinghouse Electric and Manufacturing Company in East Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 位于宾夕法尼亚州东匹兹堡的西屋电气制造公司的K.A.

sentences.en: We shall now broadcast the election returns.
sentences.zh: 我们现在播报选举结果.

sentences.en: The station launched by broadcasting the returns of the Harding-Cox presidential election.
sentences.zh: 该电台通过播报哈定与科克斯总统大选的结果开播.

sentences.en: There were no recordings of that broadcast, but in the late 1930s, the original announcer, Leah Rosenberg, made this recreation.
sentences.zh: 当时没有那次广播的录音，但在20世纪30年代末，最初的播音员莉亚·罗森伯格进行了这次重现.

sentences.en: We'd appreciate it if anyone hearing this broadcast would communicate with us, as we are very anxious to know how far the broadcast is reaching.
sentences.zh: 如果我们听到任何人收听这个广播，请与我们联系，因为我们非常渴望知道这个广播的传播范围有多远.

sentences.en: Well, nobody had ever heard of such a thing before.
sentences.zh: 好吧，以前从来没有人听说过这种事.

sentences.en: You had to wait until the next day to find out who won the election.
sentences.zh: 你必须等到第二天才能知道谁赢了选举.

sentences.en: Harry Mills, who was 13 by this time, remembers going down to the local newspaper, where they had set up a receiving station.
sentences.zh: 此时已经13岁的哈里·米尔斯记得自己去了当地报社，他们在那里设立了一个接收站.

sentences.en: Somebody would sit at the receiver, and a crowd gathered outside, or a number of people, and they would watch these returns being updated as the numbers came in bigger.
sentences.zh: 有人坐在接收器前，外面聚集了一群人，或者许多人，他们看着这些随着数字不断变大而更新的选举结果.

sentences.en: The next day, in the newspaper, of course, the talk was, gee, for the first time ever, people were able to get the reports before the newspaper was printed.
sentences.zh: 第二天，报纸上讨论的当然是，天哪，破天荒第一次，人们能够在报纸印刷出来之前就得到报道.

sentences.en: I think it's very difficult for us today to imagine really quite what a magical moment this was.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们今天很难想象这究竟是一个多么神奇的时刻.

sentences.en: Susan Douglas is a professor at the University of Michigan and the author of Inventing American Broadcasting.
sentences.zh: 苏珊·道格拉斯是密歇根大学的教授，也是《发明美国广播》的作者.

sentences.en: She says the KDKA election broadcast was a watershed event.
sentences.zh: 她说KDKA的选举广播是一个分水岭事件.

sentences.en: And because there were no connecting wires, because there was this concept of the ether, there was kind of a cosmic connection for people.
sentences.zh: 而且因为没有连接线，因为存在这种“以太”的概念，人们产生了一种宇宙般的联系.

sentences.en: It was a quasi-sort of spiritual event that these voices were coming out of the air into your home.
sentences.zh: 这些声音从空中传入你的家中，这是一种近乎精神层面的事件.

sentences.en: And two weeks after that first transmission, Westinghouse introduced the first radio for the general public, the Areola Junior, which sold for $25.
sentences.zh: 在那次首次广播两周后，西屋公司推出了面向公众的第一台收音机，名为“小光环”，售价25美元.

sentences.en: The broadcasting boom had begun, and over the next few years, radio would move out of the garage and into the living room.
sentences.zh: 广播热潮已经开始，在接下来的几年里，无线电将从车库走向起居室.

sentences.en: Today, KDKA is considered the oldest radio station in the country.
sentences.zh: 今天，KDKA被认为是该国最古老的广播电台.

sentences.en: History has not been as kind to Frank Conrad's garage.
sentences.zh: 历史对弗兰克·康拉德的车库就没有那么仁慈了.

sentences.en: This fall, bulldozers began to clear the site.
sentences.zh: 今年秋天，推土机开始清理这片场地.

sentences.en: It will soon be a Wendy's.
sentences.zh: 它很快就会变成一家温斯顿汉堡店.
推土机摧毁了康拉德的房子.

sentences.en: But Rick Harris and a group of supporters called the Conrad Project managed to save the garage, piece by piece.
sentences.zh: 但里克·哈里斯和一个名为“康拉德项目”的支持者群体设法一块一块地挽救了那个车库.

sentences.en: The woodwork, all of the doors, the windows, and some 25,000 or so bricks, the ones that survived anyway.
sentences.zh: 木工制品、所有的门、窗户，以及大约25000块砖头，也就是那些幸存下来的砖.

sentences.en: It's just the more I learn about Frank Conrad and what he did and the fact that he's virtually unknown outside of Pittsburgh,
sentences.zh: 只是我越是了解弗兰克·康拉德和他的所作所为，以及他在匹兹堡以外几乎默默无闻的事实

sentences.en: it's just something that feels that he's been overlooked for what he did.
sentences.zh: 就越觉得他的贡献被忽视了.

sentences.en: Some day, Harris hopes to reconstruct Conrad's garage and turn it into a museum.
sentences.zh: 哈里斯希望有一天能重建康拉德的车库并把它变成一座博物馆.

sentences.en: Frank Conrad may have helped to launch the modern broadcasting industry, but that wasn't really his vision.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克·康拉德可能帮助启动了现代广播行业，但这并不是他最初的愿景.

sentences.en: Conrad was just a talented engineer tinkering late at night in his garage, trying to connect to people through the air.
sentences.zh: 康拉德只是一个才华横溢的工程师，深夜在车库里瞎琢磨，试图通过空气与人们建立联系.

sentences.en: And that pretty well describes what 94-year-old Harry Mills is still doing every night at 10 o'clock.
sentences.zh: 这非常贴切地描述了94岁的哈里·米尔斯现在每天晚上10点仍在做的事情.
